title: WitnessCS: Anytime Environment-Signed Commits for Co-Adaptive VLA-WAM Training
hook: In reciprocal VLA-WAM training, imagined return can rise while an anytime propensity-corrected certificate of environment task-success change stays non-positive. Committing joint updates only when that certificate turns positive should increase final LIBERO and RoboCasa success under the same simulator-rollout budget.
hook_shape_rationale: Shape (a), surprising empirical reveal, is admitted because the falsification metric is final native simulator task success and the predicted direction disagrees with the rising internal imagined-return trace of the failing regime. Shape (c) was viable because the wrapper adds no learned model parameters, but it was rejected because reduced parameter count is not the candidate's load-bearing claim.

gap_closure.gap: Across the VLAW, World-Gymnast, and RISE frontier leaves, the sign of cycle-to-cycle change under physical dynamics is not identifiable from internal training traces once policy-selected observations, learned futures, and learned outcome scores move together; a jointly improving internal objective can therefore coexist with declining real success -- stakes: robot teams can spend scarce rollouts and GPU time strengthening a policy that fails more often, while scientific conclusions about self-improvement rest on a metric whose sign may reverse outside the coupled loop.
gap_closure.how_closed: Corpus support is thin for robot co-adaptation; C02 closes the gap by pairing candidate and incumbent policies on randomized matched LIBERO/RoboCasa resets scored by the environments' native success oracles, while the companion turns the propensity-corrected paired outcomes into an anytime accept-or-rollback decision.

core_mechanism: At co-training cycle k, an ordinary VLAW-style update produces an incumbent snapshot (pi_k, M_k) and a tentative joint snapshot (pi_k^+, M_k^+), where pi is a weight-accessible VLA policy, M is a weight-accessible action-conditioned video model, and neither requires gradients from the LIBERO or RoboCasa simulator. Let Q be the benchmark-provided reset distribution, let h index its existing task IDs, let q_h be Q's empirical mass for task h, and define the cycle estimand Delta_k = E_{x~Q,xi}[Y(pi_k^+;x,xi)-Y(pi_k;x,xi)], where Y is the benchmark's native binary task-success oracle and xi is the simulator stochastic seed. For every task h, d_{k,h} is the mean squared difference between the two policies' action vectors, normalized by the benchmark action bounds, on existing offline observations from that task; the targeting proposal is a_k(h)=q_h exp(beta d_{k,h})/sum_j q_j exp(beta d_{k,j}), with beta=1 by default and selected by a prespecified sweep over [0.5,2]. Each witness task is drawn from p_k(h)=(1-epsilon)a_k(h)+epsilon q_h, with epsilon=0.2 by default and selected by a prespecified sweep over [0.1,0.4], after which both policy snapshots run from the same environment reset and stochastic seed to produce D_{k,t}=Y^+_{k,t}-Y^0_{k,t} in {-1,0,1}. The logged importance-weighted witness X_{k,t}=q_h D_{k,t}/p_k(h) has conditional mean Delta_k and magnitude at most 1/epsilon under the stated randomization and correct logging assumptions, so no derivative, surrogate gradient, or response-mode sensitivity from the black-box simulator is required. With total one-sided false-commit risk alpha=0.05 fixed before training, the computable certificate is L_{k,t}=t^{-1}sum_{s<=t}X_{k,s}-epsilon^{-1}sqrt(2 log(k(k+1)t(t+1)/alpha)/t), whose alpha allocation over both cycles and optional stopping times follows from sum_n 1/[n(n+1)]=1. The joint snapshot is atomically committed as the next (pi_{k+1},M_{k+1}) only when L_{k,t}>m_min, where m_min=0 by default and is raised only to a deployment-specified minimum useful success gain; if the per-cycle cap B_k=128 paired witnesses is reached first, the tentative pair is rolled back, with B_k reduced uniformly across cycles when required by the declared simulator budget. Thus the controlled instance set blocks self-selected internal evidence, and the sequential-test reframe converts its independent environment outcomes into the actual downstream parameter path rather than a post-hoc score.
core_mechanism_reasoning:
BLOCK 1 - PREMISES LEDGER
P1: LIBERO and RoboCasa reset seeds, task IDs, and native success predicates define a nameable environment-level evaluation population; this is standard benchmark infrastructure, but conclusions are scoped to those simulators rather than claimed as exact real-robot guarantees.
P2: Paired common-random-number rollouts reduce variance without changing the mean candidate-versus-incumbent success difference; this is believed because both policies receive the same reset and simulator randomness before their action trajectories diverge.
P3: observation-model: task h is sampled from the logged mixture p_k, the reset is then sampled from Q conditional on h, and both policy outcomes are observed; raw witnesses are deliberately biased toward changed-policy tasks, but positivity from epsilon>0 and the logged q_h/p_k(h) weight make the stated estimator conditionally unbiased for Q when logging and reset sampling are correct.
P4: Each tentative snapshot remains fixed while its witness stream is accumulated, while witness stopping and later cycles may depend on all earlier outcomes; this makes the bounded martingale certificate applicable to the repeated adaptive loop.
P5: A positive environment-signed certificate, rather than an internal imagined-return increase, improves the final committed policy path - untested - falsification target.
P6: The VLAW policy and action-conditioned video-model implementation exposes weights and action outputs, while LIBERO/RoboCasa are used only through reset, step, and native-success calls; this access pattern is available in the stated setup.
ESTIMAND: Delta_k is the average binary task-success difference between the frozen tentative and incumbent policies over the benchmark reset distribution Q and simulator randomness xi at cycle k; L_{k,t} is a simultaneous lower confidence bound for this exact cycle-local quantity, not for real-robot success or world-model prediction error.
BLOCK 2 - NAIVE-BASELINE AUDIT
Branch (i): the runnable naive version selects tasks where the current WAM or policy predicts the largest improvement, averages the resulting paired success differences, and commits when that mean is positive; it silently assumes the adaptively selected tasks are representative of Q, which is false precisely because the co-adaptive system chooses the evidence stream. WitnessCS confronts that failure with a logged exploration mixture, propensity weighting, matched black-box outcomes, and an anytime bound before atomic commit. Importance weighting and confidence sequences are standard tools, but the domain-specific structure is that the same changing policy-WAM pair generates the candidate and the high-change task proposal, paired closed-loop trajectories cease to share states after their actions diverge, and policy plus WAM must commit atomically across repeatedly stopped cycles; the contribution is this executable proposal/evidence firewall for reciprocal robot learning, not a new generic concentration inequality.
BLOCK 3 - DESIGN RATIONALE
Only the cycle-sign gap was selected because its paired witness stream is independently runnable and the other gaps would require residual-mode or censoring machinery not needed for the commit claim. A residual-mode surgery design was rejected because its load-bearing producer would require an unavailable derivative through a black-box simulator, generic cross-fitting was rejected because it does not fix the adaptive target distribution, and a fixed phase scaffold was rejected because an interleaved sequential commit rule can spend evidence only until the current candidate is decided. The chosen design draws on controlled intervention outcomes, a source not occupied by DAgger, conservative MBRL, target networks, or generic cross-fitting in the lineage.
core_mechanism_steps:
1. Instantiate a VLAW-style co-training reproduction with weight-accessible VLA policy pi_k and action-conditioned video model M_k on existing LIBERO and RoboCasa trajectories; input is the incumbent checkpoint pair and output is a tentative updated pair (pi_k^+, M_k^+) plus the unchanged incumbent snapshots.
2. Build Q directly from the benchmarks' task/reset samplers and cache existing offline reset observations by task ID; input is benchmark metadata and stored observations, and output is q_h and normalized action-divergence scores d_{k,h} from forward passes of pi_k and pi_k^+.
3. Compute a_k and the randomized mixture p_k with the declared beta and epsilon, sample a task and reset, and log h, q_h, p_k(h), reset seed, simulator seed, checkpoint hashes, and rollout order; input is the divergence table and output is a reproducible witness request.
4. Query LIBERO or RoboCasa twice as a black box from that matched request, once with each frozen policy in randomized order, and read the native task-success predicates; input is the witness request and output is the paired outcome D_{k,t}, which changes downstream behavior only through the later joint commit decision.
5. Append X_{k,t}=q_h D_{k,t}/p_k(h), recompute L_{k,t}, and persist the audit row; input is the paired outcome plus logged propensity and output is the load-bearing certificate, with no simulator differentiation or learned outcome judge.
6. If L_{k,t}>m_min, atomically promote both tentative checkpoints so pi_k^+ generates the next real/simulated actions and M_k^+ generates the next imagined futures; otherwise request another witness until B_k, then restore both incumbent hashes so the failed update cannot affect later rollouts or training data.
7. Repeat Steps 1-6 for later co-training cycles while retaining the global alpha schedule; input is the last committed pair and prior audit log, and output is a final policy checkpoint whose complete update ancestry is environment-signed.
8. Run matched-budget ordinary VLAW-style training, unweighted targeted-witness gating, label-permuted-certificate gating, and an exhaustive-Q oracle gate; input is identical initial checkpoints and seeds, and output is final native task success plus commit/rollback traces for mechanism falsification.
falsification_prediction: Starting from the same VLAW-style policy/world-model checkpoints, run matched-budget co-training on LIBERO and RoboCasa under ordinary alternating updates, WitnessCS, and the controls, then measure final native simulator task-success rate and the sign agreement between each L_{k,t} decision and an exhaustive-Q evaluation of that candidate. If the mechanism works, final task-success rate increases and harmful joint commits decrease relative to ordinary co-training, especially in runs where imagined return rises while exhaustive-Q success falls. The single load-bearing variable is the environment-signed lower certificate L_{k,t}; as a negative control, randomly swap candidate/incumbent labels within each collected pair before recomputing L while leaving every rollout and budget unchanged, which should return final task success toward the ordinary co-training baseline rather than merely changing L itself. As a positive control, replace L with the exhaustive-Q candidate-versus-incumbent success difference, which should preserve the direction of the downstream benefit while upper-bounding attainable commit accuracy.
compute_budget: Approximately 32 80GB-class GPU-days for matched LIBERO/RoboCasa co-training, paired witness rollouts, controls, and iteration; $0 paid-API cost because native benchmark success predicates replace external judges. This is comfortable within the stated <=50 GPU-day and ~$10k API envelope.

differentiation_from_lit.delta: VLAW alternates real-rollout world-model refinement with synthetic policy improvement, whereas WitnessCS constructs logged randomized candidate/incumbent environment pairs and an anytime lower success bound that atomically governs whether either tentative checkpoint enters the next cycle (abstract-only inference).

World-Gymnast optimizes a VLA inside video dynamics using a learned VLM reward, while WitnessCS measures each proposed update with paired native-environment success and corrects the deliberately nonuniform task allocation before commit (abstract-only inference).

RISE composes a future predictor and progress-value model into imagined advantages, but it does not construct a propensity-corrected paired environment estimand or use its anytime sign to accept or roll back the joint learner state (abstract-only inference).

WorldSync aligns predicted intervention effects with ground-truth futures to improve action faithfulness, whereas WitnessCS measures the downstream candidate-versus-incumbent task-success difference and makes that independent sign the update commit primitive (abstract-only inference).

what_step_was_missed: VLAW would have needed to execute candidate and incumbent policies from randomized matched benchmark resets with logged allocation probabilities, convert their paired native-success differences into a cycle-uniform anytime lower bound, and atomically condition the next policy/world-model state on that bound.
